newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Small firms to create 50,500 new Irish jobs in 199.
newsitem.headline: Small firms to create 50,500 new Irish jobs in 199.

text.p: Irish small firms association, SFA, said on Monday the sector expected to create 50,500 new jobs in 1997, compared to 43,000 in 1996.
Small firms, employing less than 50 people, accounted for 403,500 of the country's total 1996 private sector employment of 807,000, SFA director, Brendan Butler said in a statement.
But Butler said the sector was experiencing difficulties in recruiting staff mainly due to people's preference to remain on social welfare.
"Many small firms are seeing the Social Welfare/Tax Systems as their greatest competitor in recruiting new employees," Butler said.

"This week's budget must have a clear focus on increasing take home pay of low paid workers and removing the disincentive to social welfare recipients to actively seek employment and move into the legitimate sector of the economy," he said.

The SFA said Ireland's positive economic conditions of increased consumer demand, low inflation and interest rates, special loan schemes, reduction in employer PRSI among others, continued to contribute to the small sector's growth.
